items.title: Greg Thomas interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 2014
items.q: The interviewee responds to the interviewer's mention of Herb Alpert by agreeing with the classification of his music ('Right. And that’s okay.'), but provides no personal interaction, meeting, or professional connection.

ctx.x: Absolutely. And a disservice to a public who may not know jazz history. And if you are either calling yourself a jazz musician or allowing yourself, because you are an instrumentalist say, to actually be called a jazz musician and you’re not that — Kenny G is not a jazz musician. I’m not saying Kenny G can’t play. Kenny G has a nice tone on the soprano sax, and I don’t mean to just — you know there’s a group of people who just knee jerk condemnation of certain people and Kenny G is one of them. But I’m using him…
Herb Alpert. When I was a kid he was, and in fact I read a fact recently that Kenny G surpassed Herb Alpert as the largest selling instrumentalist. But Herb Alpert, no one © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-
called him a jazz musician. He was playing instrumental pop music and it was very pleasant and stuff. So let’s just call Kenny G an instrumental pop musician.
